title: Automated compliance evidence pipeline: data-residency, retention proofs & role attestation exports
creator: Marco Li
description:
Background:
Customers in regulated markets require tamper-evident proof that: (1) their data was stored only in specific regions (data residency), (2) retention policies were applied and expired data deleted or archived per policy (retention), and (3) access to sensitive controls and data is limited and periodically attested (RBAC + access review). Currently we have partial artifacts: per-request region metadata, retention TTL logs in backend services, and SCIM provisioning audit logs. There is no unified, automatable evidence export that ties these signals together into an auditable package for legal/regulatory review or for our SOC/Pg/Mgmt customer requests.

Scope & Goals:
- Produce a reproducible, signed "evidence bundle" per customer or per compliance period that contains residency proofs, retention enforcement logs, and role/access attestation records.
- Support export formats: compressed NDJSON + manifest (SHA256 checksums), and a ready-to-upload ZIP for customer/third-party auditors.
- Automate scheduled exports (daily/weekly/monthly) and on-demand exports triggered by compliance teams or account owners.
- Include mappings between RBAC roles and data residency-scoped resources (e.g., which roles have cross-region access).
- Integrate evidence generation with existing SCIM/SAML audit streams and with KMS key access logs for encryption-at-rest proof.
- Ensure privacy: export only customer-scoped records; scrub unrelated tenant metadata.

High-level design (implementation notes):
- Ingestion: build a small pipeline (Lambda + SQS or K8s job) that pulls: storage region metadata (object-level or logical location), retention enforcement logs (deletes, TTL expirations), SCIM provisioning events, SSO/SAML assertion logs, and KMS key use events.
- Correlation: unify events by customer_id and time window. Produce a manifest that lists each file, SHA256, and a JSONL index mapping resource -> events.
- Signing: sign the manifest with an internal signing key (rotateable) and optionally produce an HSM-backed timestamped signature for SOC use.
- Export formats: NDJSON files per signal (residency.ndjson, retention.ndjson, rbac-attestations.ndjson), a manifest.json (flat JSON with checksums and high-level summary), and a metrics CSV for ingestion into security dashboards.
- UI/Console: extend Console exports page with a "Compliance Evidence" flow: choose period, choose scope (customer / org / workspace), export frequency and retention for the evidence bundle.
- Access controls: only users with "compliance:export" scope (admin/owner) can run on-demand exports. Export blobs stored in an S3 bucket (customer-evidence) with lifecycle and encryption; pre-signed URL available for download for 7 days by default.

Acceptance criteria:
- A scheduled weekly export for a sandbox workspace is generated automatically and passes ingestion validation (manifest checksums match contents).
- Manual on-demand export by an account owner completes within SLA (under 10 minutes for medium-sized customers up to 100k events in window).
- Export includes at least: object location events, retention-delete events, SCIM provisioning/deprovisioning events, SAML assertions summary, and KMS key-use entries when requested.
- Manifest signing is verifiable with public key (documented in Confluence).
- Audit UI shows export history with status, size, and SHA256 fingerprints.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Prototype pipeline ingesting logs from test cluster and generate proof bundles for internal sandbox customers (Cycle 1).
2) Add RBAC mapping service endpoint and Console export UI (Cycle 2).
3) Pilot with 3 enterprise customers who require residency proofs (Cycle 3) and collect performance metrics.
4) General availability and documentation release, including how to validate bundle signatures (Cycle 4).

Monitoring & observability:
- Export job success rate, mean latency, bundle size, and manifest verification failures.
- Alert on >1 export failure in 24h for any production tenant.
- Integrate export delivery metrics into Console and into PagerDuty for on-call.

Open technical trade-offs / risks:
- Snapshot consistency: across distributed storage and services, achieving perfect point-in-time consistency is expensive. We will document the time-window guarantees and include high-water marks for each signal.
- Cost: generating frequent full exports for large customers can be costly; consider incremental deltas after initial full export.
- Sensitive data leakage: we must ensure exported events are filtered to customer scope and scrub PII not required for compliance.
- Signing trust model: whether to provide customers with our public key or integrate cross-signer (customer-provided) verification.

Next steps (short term):
- Spike: wire up a PoC pipeline to pull SCIM events and object location metadata and produce a signed manifest (owner: Aisha).
- Data model: finalize NDJSON schema for three signals and manifest spec (owner: Marco).
- Console mock: PM/DX to produce a minimal export UI prototype and identify permission model.

2026-03-01 - Aisha Kapoor: PoC progress: successfully ingested SCIM delta stream for test-org and wrote residency.ndjson with per-object region metadata. Manifest SHA256 generation verified in local tests. Opening PR for POC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compliance-evidence/pull/12
2026-03-04 - Sofia Ramirez (Compliance): Confirmed required attestations for EU data residency audits; asked to include KMS key-use logs. Noted legal prefers HSM-signed manifests if possible.

2026-03-07 - Security (Ravi Patel): Reviewed PoC design. Recommended use of a rotateable signing key in KMS and an immutable export S3 bucket with Object Lock for 30 days for internal retention. Also requested threat model doc before GA.

2026-03-10 - Aisha Kapoor: Performance test update: sample export for 50k events produced 120MB bundle; manifest creation + sign took ~4s; upload to S3 + pre-signed URL generation measured at ~30s. Next: add filtering to ensure tenant scoping and incremental export delta logic.
